title: Player showed 0:00/0:00 until Play was pressed, even when audio was ready
description:
The player's <audio> element used preload="none", so the browser never
fetched metadata (including duration) until playback actually started. The
time display stayed 0:00 / 0:00 until the reader pressed Play, even once
the audio was fully generated and its URL known -- reported live on
Pilobol.us for a 9:09 clip.

First attempt at a fix was wrong and briefly shipped (commit 39fa5d0, since
corrected): it read the job record's duration_seconds field and displayed
that as clip length. That field is actually claim-to-completion
*processing* time (now_epoch - claimed_epoch in the router's _mark_done,
also surfaced as avg_duration_seconds in the admin overview as a perf
metric) -- unrelated in magnitude to how long the resulting audio runs. For
the 9:09 clip above it showed '0:07', a confident wrong number, worse than
the 0:00 placeholder it replaced. Caught and corrected within the same
session before it was reported as fixed.

Actual fix (commit 55bae3d): there is no field anywhere that carries real
clip length; the only correct source is the audio file's own header.
Switched <audio> to preload="metadata" (fetches just the header via a small
range request) and added an explicit .load() call once src is set, since
some browsers don't start that fetch on their own for an element that
already existed before src changed. Self-contained to the embed, no
backend/CDK changes. Covered by a new test in embed/tests/player.test.ts.
